text: |-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Wing Necklaces are Accessories in and . The common variant can be purchased from the Hilltop Caravan. The Devotional Necklace is a direct upgrade to this accessory. In , the legendary variant can be obtained from Hilltop Chegwin.
The Watchpoint Bridge (Japanese: , Monomi no Ipponbashi) is a Landmark in . It is located on Melnath's Shoulder in the Aetia Region.
The West Perimeter Gate (Japanese: , Gaikaku Nishi Gēto) is a Location in . It is located at the Agnus Castle Barbican. It is the western gate of the facility.
Watchtower No. 1 (Japanese: , Daiichi Kanshutō) is a Location in . It is located in the Perimeter Woodland in Li Garte Prison Camp.

Well-Plated Zelinka (Japanese: , Kōkaku no Zerika) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Crustip family, and can be found at level 53 in the Svinne Cavity of Yzana Plains. The Ultranull Shield Skill can be earned by the Soulhacker class for defeating it.

Widdershins Radler (Japanese: , Kikō no Radorā) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Eluca family, and can be found at level 48 at Anu Shoals in the Erythia Sea. The Awakilling Skill can be earned by the Soulhacker class by defeating it.
The West Gate Road (Japanese: , Nishi Gēto-dōri) is a Landmark in . It is located at Fort O'Virbus on the Syra Hovering Reefs.
The Windstrong Bluffs (Japanese: , Kazeoi no Gakemichi) is a Landmark in , located in High Maktha Wildwood in the Pentelas Region. It leads to the Penshia Portal on the Syra Hovering Reefs.
Where The Heart Is (Japanese: , Omoi no Arika) is a Hero Quest in , dedicated to Zeon.
White Melonballs are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Pentelas Region. It can also be purchased from Sunny & Cheerio's Caravan, or produced from the Cascade Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Wiltflowers are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Aetia Region. They can also be produced from the Hillside Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Wetstones are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Keves Castle Region. They can also be produced from the Perimeter Outlet Fabricator after the first step of Colony 0 renovation.

Well-Dressed Maktha Salads are Meal items in . They can be cooked by Manana at Rest Spots. 1 Silver Nopon Coin can be used to cook this meal instead of the necessary ingredients. It can be unlocked by purchasing the Maktha Ever-Greens from the Colony Tau Canteen for the first time.
The Wilderness Caravan is a shop in . It is run by a Traderpon and can be found at the Lake Rezzento Camp in the Eagus Wilderness.
Wheelideeli's Abacus is a Key Item in . It is obtained from the Staahl Gogol during the quest Prison Refurbishment.
Wett Upas are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Upa family, and can be found at level 45-47 in Loska's Cavern on the Urayan Trail, or at level 58-59 at Cape Arcaphor in Erythia Sea.
Why So Busy? is a Standard Quest in . Upon completion of this quest, Missing in Action is automatically accepted.

Wheelideeli is a Nopon NPC in . He is a merchant formerly affiliated with the Nopon Caravans, and does trade with Colony 0. He becomes a merchant vendor in Li Garte Prison Camp after completing the quest Prison Refurbishment, operating the Shop named Handypon.
Widow (Japanese: ) is a NPC in . Widow can be found in Colony 11.
Whole Wild Lobsters are Meal items in . They can be purchased from the Michiba Canteen. Purchasing it for the first time unlocks the recipe for the Saucy-Glossy Gem Lobster for Manana's Menu.

Where We Belong is the ending theme of . It was composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. Although Tetsuya Takahashi came up with the original lyrics, the English translation was provided by Lisa Gomamoto. Sara Weeda lent her voice for the song. Where We Belong is also featured as an available karaoke song in Karaoke JOYSOUND for Nintendo Switch.

Wind Sickle (Japanese: , Kamaitachi) is a Talent Art in . It is an Art exclusive to Ashera with no equivalent available to the Ouroboros. She spins her double-edged sword above herself then twirls and does a hard slash.
Wild Wave is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Soulhacker class. It is acquired by defeating the Unique Monster while the Soul Hack skill is set on any player-controlled party member.

Water Jet is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Soulhacker class. It is acquired by defeating the Unique Monster Wraithfin Segna while the Soul Hack skill is set on any player-controlled party member.

The Waterlogged Daksha Shrine (Japanese: , Suibotsushita Dakusha Shinden) is a Location in , located in Raguel Lake on The Ragmos Desolation. It is the remnants of the Daksha Shrine submerged in Raguel Lake. There is a Relic found here containing an Affinity Growth Unlock Kit.

The West Planada Panorama (Japanese: , Nishi Puranada Kanshi Chiten) is a location in , located past the Diablada Cliffs on the Aurora Shelf. The Panorama Camp is located here. There is an Agnian Outpost located here starting in Chapter 4.
The Waypoint Sapling (Japanese: , Shinju no Shihyō) is a location in , located on the Aurora Shelf.
Wickt Ignas are Quest Exclusive Bosses in . They are members of the Igna family that are fought at level 23 in the Exile Fortress Ruins on the Aurora Shelf during Riku's Workshop.
Watchful Valencia (Japanese: , Kanshi no Barenshia) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Rhogul family, and can be found at level 10 in Ragrinar Passage on the Aurora Shelf.

Where We Used To Be is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track four of disc two from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track four of disc seven from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. It is a piano arrangement of Elysium, in the Blue Sky. This song plays on the title screen for , as well as during the following moments: * Rex and Nia's conversation on the C.S.E.V. Maelstrom. * Rex convincing Nia to stay with the party following their escape from Mòrag and Brighid. * Vandham's explanation of how Blades return to their Core Crystals upon the death of their Driver. * Cole revealing himself as a Flesh Eater. * Rex telling Pyra about how his parents died when h

White All Around Us is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track twenty of disc five from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track twenty of disc ten from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. It is a remix of Xenoblade II - Where It All Began -, and uses a motif from Elysium, in the Blue Sky. This song plays during the first part of the game's credits. It also plays when the party meets Shulk and Fiora in the Land of Challenge.
White Whale Parts are three Important Items in . They are collected at Northpointe Beach in Primordia during the course of We Were Soldiers.
The Weapon Test Data is an Important Item in . It is collected from the Skell Wreckage treasure at Rust Lake in Noctilum during the course of Data Miner.
Widebeams are shoulder weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Titan Missile type Galdrs, Gularth or Sylooth.
Weather Immunity is a buff in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It grants the character immunity to all weather effects (spores, lightning, sandstorm).
Weather Damage: Heat is a debuff in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It inflicts thermal damage at regular intervals.
Weather Damage: Lightning is a debuff in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It inflicts electric damage at regular intervals.
Waypoint Market (Japanese: , Shuppatsu no Ichiba) is a Location in . It is located in Garfont Village in the Kingdom of Uraya. There are multiple shops found here.

, known in Japan as Xenoblade (Japanese: , Zenobureido), is a role-playing video game published by Nintendo and developed by Monolith Soft for the Wii console. The game was announced during E3 2009, when a trailer was released to media. The trailer shows a futuristic sword-wielding character battling giant robots and creatures as well as third-person exploration gameplay. In January 2010, the game was renamed from Monado: Beginning of the World to Xenoblade to honor Tetsuya Takahashi, "who poured his soul into making this and who has been working on the Xeno series". The game was released on June 10, 2010 in Japan, and released on August 19, 2011 in PAL regions. The game was released in Nort

Yellow Antols are enemies in . They are members of the Antol family, along with the fiercer Red Antol. They can be found north of Watchpoint Junction, or on the Splintered Path before the events at Mechonis Core. Four of them must be defeated to complete Safety First, given by Daza in Colony 6.
Worn Muscle Fibres are materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Orluga in Makna Forest, or traded for.
Yusa (Japanese: , Yushi) is a Nopon in Xenoblade Chronicles. He is one of two nopon doctors - Medi's rival - and can be found in the Underground Store of Frontier Village.

The Yellow Flower Grove (Japanese: , Kiiro no Hanabatake) is a location in . It is located in Makna Forest, northeast of the Glowmoss Trihenge and southeast of Clear Waterfall. As its name suggests, there are many yellow flowers. Several quests can be completed here.

Yaldabaoth (Japanese: , Yarudabaoto; English dub: ), also known as Gold Face (Japanese: , Ōgon no Feisu), is a Faced Mechon in . It is a key antagonist of the game and serves as the true leader of the Faced Mechon. Yaldaboth can control any Mechon at will using this armour. It is the largest and strongest Faced Mechon ever built.

Yellow Cats (Japanese: , Ierō Kyatto) are collectables in . They can be found in the Ether Mine. According to their description, they are also known as the Golden Lightning and they have smooth lemon yellow paw-pads.
Xekit (Japanese: , Jeki) is a Machina in Xenoblade Chronicles. She can be found at the Ether Light of the Hidden Machina Village.

Wool Rocks (Japanese: , Ūru Rokku) are collectables in . They can be found in Satorl Marsh. According to their description, they are rocks covered in black fur that can be shorn to make blankets. Three are required for Making Camp.

Yolkless Flamii Eggs are rare materials in . They can be dropped by low-level Flamii in Colony 9, or traded for with Jackson. According to their description, they hatch without fertilisation, which is an unexplained miracle. One is needed for Colony 9's Material Quest 4.

※ After this quest is completed, Gerugu may offer another quest, With Even More Gratitude. With Much Gratitude (Japanese: , Saijōkyū no Kansha) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Batubatu in the Traveller's Rest on Bionis' Leg. If Shulk is in the active party, he will comment.

※ After this quest is completed, Gerugu may offer another quest, Legend of Mythical Empress. With Even More Gratitude (Japanese: , Sai: Saijōkyū no Kansha) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Gerugu in the Traveller's Rest on Bionis' Leg. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment.
Wolf Guarders (Japanese: , Urufugādā) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are gunlances wielded by Reyn.
Wyvern Cutlasses (Japanese: , Unryūfūkotō) are weapons in . They are swords wielded by Dunban, and can be dropped by several high level enemies. They are swords with the highest minimum attack.
The Wrecking Nibblers (Japanese: , Hakai no Bakubaku) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are biters wielded by Riki. They can be purchased at the Frontier Village Weapon Shop for 9,960 G.

Wisdom Rods (Japanese: , Waizuroddo, Wise Rod) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are staves that can be wielded by Melia. They can be acquired by purchasing them at Colony 6 Shop 7 for 23,640 G.

Yellow Pollens are Key Items in Xenoblade Chronicles. The party is asked to collect five of them from the Yellow Flower Grove by Dobadoba, for Pollen Orb Ingredients. They will be used to make Pollen Orbs for Frontier Village.

Wisp Glow Sticks are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Bunker Wisps in Colony 6 during a clear night or the Dim Wisp in Tephra Cave, which only appears during Jackson the Poet. They can also be traded for with Daza and Talonyth if he moves to Colony 6. According to their description, they are light-emitting sticks that are used in artillery guidance systems. Five of them are needed for A Gift For Miko.

Wreckage Beach (Japanese: , Zangai no Sunabe) is a landmark in . It is located on the Fallen Arm, and is a long beach area, directly connected to the Transformer Area. It has three locations on it: Zakt Spring, Jifum Beach and Silver Wreckage. It is the beach that Shulk and Fiora land upon after falling from Galahad Fortress, and the first location visited on the Fallen Arm. As its name suggests, it is littered in the remains of fallen Mechon, presumably also from the Fortress or Sword Valley. It is inhabited by Oros Krabbles and Kukukoro Flamii and by the Prosperous Zepar, a Unique Monster. After the events at the Mechonis Core it also becomes home to one of the five Superbosses — the

World's Strongest Flavour (Japanese: , Sekaiichi Koikuchi no Ryōri) is a quest in . It can be received from Kofuko in the armour shop at the Central Plaza in Frontier Village. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment. This quest and Reversed Tastes are mutually exclusive.

Wrathful Orobas (Japanese: , Gekirin no Orobasu) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a Mechon, and can be found at level 67 southeast of the Dios Pillar on floor 1F of Agniratha. The party must defeat the Wrathful Orobas to complete the Military Status 2 - 2 timed quest.

Wise Gremory (Japanese: , Sōmei no Guremori) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a Mechon, and can be found at level 68 on the bridge west of the Meyneth Statue in Agniratha. Defeating it is the objective of the Military Status 1 - 2 timed quest.

Wool Seluas (Japanese: , Ūru Serura) are enemies in . They are members of the Selua family, and can be found at level 73 in Bionis' Interior. They drop the Steel Selua Cells needed for Colony 6 Reconstruction.

Wisp Bliss Rings are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Tramont Wisps at Digit 2 on the Fallen Arm and the Bright Wisp, or traded for with Voltak. According to their description, they emit a faint pink light to highlight the wearer's happiness. Two are needed to complete Betrothal Test (En Argentis).

The Wizard Entia (Japanese: , Wizu Entā) is a story exclusive enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles. She is a High Entia, and is fought in Alcamoth once, when the party is attacked in their quarters by a group of assassins of the Bionite Order.

Woeful Upas (Japanese: , Kafuku no Ūpā) are quest exclusive enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found in Satorl Marsh in the water above Zaldania Waterfall. They are kindred enemies, and appear as a group of five with group loyalty. They first appear during A Final Sweet Favour, attacking the party after the Mysterious Droplet is obtained. It is not required to defeat them during the quest. They will respawn after the quest is completed, they are thus one of the rare quest exclusive enemies which respawn after the related quest completion.

Yumea's Maid is a High Entia in Xenoblade Chronicles. She appears after Melancholy Tyrea, and can be found on the outside entrance to Junks while it is parked in Colony 6. She is the maid of Yumea, the first consort of the High Entia Emperor Sorean. She can be found at the conclusion of Melancholy Tyrea. If spoken to, she will describe further backstory to the relationship of Yumea and Tyrea, and their heartfelt goodbye in light of Yumea's condition. She seems to serve no other purpose than to further detail the relationship that Yumea and Tyrea had, cannot be traded with, and does not appear on the Affinity Chart. Strangely, she appears as one of the gossiping NPCs during a vision when acce

Wisp Sun Beads are rare materials in . They can only be dropped by Femuny Wisps in Tephra Cave, and cannot be traded for. According to their description, they are eternally shining beads that bring exponential growth to plant life. One Wisp Sun Bead is needed for Replica Monado 3.
The Worship Terrace is a location in . It is located on the third floor of Agniratha, near the Shrine Transporter.
Worn-Out Weapons are common materials in . They can be dropped by Tirkins.

, known in Japan as XenobladeX (Japanese: , Zenobureido Kurosu, literally Xenoblade Cross), is a role-playing video game developed by Monolith Soft and published by Nintendo for the Wii U console. It was released on April 29, 2015 in Japan and on December 4, 2015 in North America and Europe. The game was announced under the tentative title of "X" in a Nintendo Direct in January 2013. Prior to the 2014 E3 show, little was known about the game other than that it followed a similar style of in its battle style and exploration themes. During E3 2014, a Nintendo Treehouse demo of the game included commentary which suggested that while it retains the name, it was more of a spiritual successor of w

Young Grexes (Japanese: , Yangu Rupusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Grex family. They can be found at level 6-10 at the East Gate Plain or at Grieving Plains in Primordia.

Wood Lepyx (Japanese: , Uddo Fontera) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Lepyx family, and can be found at level 4-10 at East Gate Plain or at Sayram Lake in Primordia.

is a role-playing video game published by Nintendo and developed by Monolith Soft and co-developed by Monster Games for the New Nintendo 3DS. It is a port of the original . The game was announced during a Japanese Nintendo Direct presentation on August 29, 2014. The game was released on April 2, 2015 in Japan and Europe, and in North America on April 10, 2015.

The Wonderment Bluff (Japanese: , Dōmoku no Gake) is an Unexplored Territory in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia. This is a spot that overlooks Noctilum and can be accessed by the top left corner of the hexagon to the top left of FN Site 103. As with all Unexplored Territories, its discovery yields an achievement ("Wonders of Wonderment Bluff").

Worker Arachnos (Japanese: , Wākā Supaido) are six story exclusive enemies in . They are members of the Arachno family, and can be found in Tephra Cave between the Spring of Grief and Vilia Lake. After Shulk and Reyn find the bodies of some traders by a small unnamed pond, there is a story event battle in which they are attacked by six Worker Arachnos and two Director Arachnos. These six Worker Arachnos are level 7 Kindred Enemies which drop no Treasure Chests, do not respawn, and detect by sight at a 120° angle, to a distance of 21 meters. There is a normal variant. These Worker Arachnos are level 8, non-kindred monsters, respawn normally, drop Treasure Chests, and detect by sound at a 360°

Young Ciniculas (Japanese: , Yūsu Vasaruto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Cinicula family, and can be found at level 15-18 at FN Site 117 in Primordia. Two of them must be defeated during Mission B.

Your Voice is a track in Xenoblade Chronicles X, composed and arranged by Hiroyuki Sawano with lyrics by [http://myanimelist.net/people/26119/mpi mpi] and vocals provided by Mika Kobayashi. It is track 12 of disc one from the XenobladeX Original Soundtrack. This music is heard in the ending of the main storyline and it continues to play in the credits.

Wir fliegen is a track in composed and arranged by Hiroyuki Sawano with vocals provided by Cyua, and lyrics written by Rie. It is track 13 of disc one from the XenobladeX Original Soundtrack. This music is heard whenever the party leader is in Overdrive. The only songs that aren't replaced by "Wir fliegen" are 2XDLB or The key we've lost . In , this song plays while Overdrive is active.

Wise Apricas (Japanese: , Waizu Dometomu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Aprica family, and can be found at level 28-30 on Keegan Ridge or the River Isle in Oblivia. They are tall deer-like enemies. They can drop the Aprica Back Moss needed to complete From Idea to Inventory as well as the Redwood Aprica Antlers needed for Mayhem.

The Wrothians (Japanese: , Rāsu, Wrath; English dub: ) are a race of beings in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are an alien race who made an alliance with the Ganglion. They have been a proud tribe of mercenaries and warriors for generations, and display a prominent samurai theme in both design and values.

Wolf (Japanese: , Urufu) is a NPC in and . He can be found at the Mission Control Board on the BLADE Concourse in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles, along with Trevor on the opposite side of Eleonora. He is a member of the Harriers Division, and provides combat tips on toppling foes and later on Skill assignment.

Yardley's Scheme (Japanese: , Yādorī no Kuwadate) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Yardley in the Outfitters Test Hangar in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles.

The Wood Tectinsula (Japanese: , Uddo Tapenta) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Tectinsula family. It can be found at level 22 in the Canopied Nightwood in Noctilum during Adventure!.

Xe-doms (Japanese: , Ze-raa) are machine enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Miran drones utilized by the Ganglion for security. They appear as huge hovering creatures made of a strange metal, with glowing lines around their bodies and a single glowing eye in the center. They can be found either patrolling or half-submerged in the ground. Often they will only be aggressive toward Skells. Xe-doms appear in all regions, but are rare outside of Sylvalum and Cauldros. Xe-doms are not affected by adverse weather.
Wood Potamuses (Japanese: , Uddo Hippo) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Potamus family, and can be found at level 27-28 in Noctilum, next to Whale's Nostril BC.

Young Simius (Japanese: , Yangu Shimiusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Simius and can be found at level 11-13 on Sickle Rock Rise and at level 19-20 at Biahno Grassland in Primordia during the day. They can drop the Muscled Simius Bulges needed for Indigen Investigation.
Wrathful Simius (Japanese: , Rasu Shimiusu, Wrath Simius) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Simius family, and can be found at level 42 or 47 at FN Site 225 in Noctilum.
Wise Progen (Japanese: , Waizu Ekuusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Progen and can be found at level 21-27 at the Oblivia Ingress.

z37b20a13t01t08le is a track in Xenoblade Chronicles X, composed and arranged by Hiroyuki Sawano. It is track nine of disc two from the XenobladeX Original Soundtrack. The first thirty seconds of this track plays when an enemy detects the party. The next section plays during certain event battles, such as: * Elder Grex accompanied by two Callow Grexes before Elma escorts Cross to New Los Angeles. * Glennar and company during Chapter 3. * Chief Qmoeva and Platoon Qmoevas during Chapter 5. * Tainted Sphinx during Chapter 6. * Ga Jiarg, Ga Buidhe, and company during Chapter 9. * Soldier Chimeras in the Lifehold Core during Chapter 12. * Brume Auravis during Renewed Will. * Fierce Vigent during

Yardley's Hideaway (Japanese: , Yādorī no Kakurega) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located below the Administrative District of New Los Angeles. This landmark is unveiled during House of Cards.
Wood Scirpos (Japanese: , Uddo Shirunea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Scirpo family, and can be found at level 31-35 or at level 38-40 at Rock Cavern in Primordia.

Yune, the Ambusher (Japanese: , Kishū no Yūnu) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Visigel family. It can rarely be found at level 20 at Seabird's Beak in Sylvalum. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Yune, the Ambusher.
Yoyotsu is an NPC in . She is a Nopon and can be found in the Whale's Nostril in Noctilum. She is met during the mission The Ties That Bind. She is one of Tatsu's sisters.
Wootz Blattas (Japanese: , Ūtsu Buratta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family. They can be found at level 23-24 at Castaway Cavern in Primordia.
Yolanda (English dub: ) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is located at Division Drive in the Administrative District. She is a member of the Prospectors Division.

Yagami's Vista (Japanese: , Yagami Ichibō) is a Scenic Viewpoint in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Noctilum, at the northern entrance to the Whale's Nostril and east of the Sapphire Carpet, reachable from FN Site 221. As with all Scenic Viewpoints, its discovery yields an achievement ("Conquering Yagami's Vista").

Yessenia, the Husky-Voiced (Japanese: , Sabigoe no Jessenia) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Mortifole family. It can be found hidden at level 23 at FN Site 221 near Garden Spring in Noctilum. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Yessenia, the Husky-Voiced.

Yggralith Zero (Japanese: , Reikō Yegirasu) is a Nemesis in . It is a level 60 Yggralith and is fought atop the Kw'arah Villa in Cauldros during the Nemesis Squad Mission The Final Menace. It can summon Filiavents for assistance.
Yardley (Japanese: , Yādorī) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found just inside the Outfitters Test Hangar in the Industrial District.
Yun'tonam is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is an Orphean who can be found at the Deliverance Park in the Residential District of New Los Angeles during the night.

The Wrothian Stronghold (Japanese: , Rāsu no Nejiro) is an area in . It is located in Oblivia, and is accessible only via a cave near FN Site 315. It is the base for the Wrothians. While the cave is accessible at any time, the party can only officially discover this area after accepting A Challenger Approaches. In the , Ga Jiarg can be found here when not in the party. There are no enemies here.

Yaya Sesames (Japanese: , Yayyagoma) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum, in particular inside the cave at FN Site 401. Four bunches of them are needed for De-stressing Delicacy.
Yabuyabu Ointments (Japanese: , Yabuyabu Kusuri) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum.

Witch Papils (Japanese: , Witchi Papirio) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Papil family, and can be found at level 22-23 at South Ciel Sandsea and at level 28-30 at Lake Ciel in Sylvalum at daytime.

Wizard Papils (Japanese: , Wizādo Papirio) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Papil family, and can be found at level 38-39 at Delusians North Summit in Sylvalum at daytime. They are under the giant flower.
Worn Muscle Fibers are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Evellos in Primordia or Monoceroses in Cauldros.

Young Blattas (Japanese: , Yangu Buratta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family. They can be found at level 41-42 at Talon Rock Third Terrane in Primordia at night. They appear randomly among the packs of Dark Blatta.

Xerns (Japanese: , Zerun) are machine enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are huge Ganglion aircraft carriers, and are some of the biggest and strongest enemies in the game. There are only five known Xerns. They do not drop any material items, but the Tyrants can drop a holofigure or equipment.

The Wrothian Enacters (Japanese: , Rāsu Ashigara) are three Main Bosses in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Wrothian warriors, and are fought at level 32 at the Shivering Sands in Sylvalum. They assist Ga Jiarg and Ga Buidhe, along with the Wrothian Sneaker at the end of Chapter 9.

The Wrothian Sneaker (Japanese: , Rāsu Shinobara) is a Main Boss in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a Wrothian warrior, and is fought at level 32 at the Shivering Sands in Sylvalum. She assists Ga Jiarg and Ga Buidhe, along with the three Wrothian Enacters at the end of Chapter 9.

Yelena, the Sequestered (, Yūjaku no Yerena) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Scirpo family. It can be found at level 34 at East Janpath Plain in Primordia. It is considerably larger than the nearby Green Scirpos.

Yuiro, the Luxuriant (Japanese: , Zakuro no Yuiro) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Blatta family. It can be found at level 51-55 at Great Nail in Noctilum, on top of a large, flat-headed pillar. It crawls out of the ground after defeating the nearby blattas.

Ya-rhat, the Thundercloud (Japanese: , Raiun no Ya-rato) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Fal-swo machine. It can be found at level 49 at Kw'arah Cloister in Cauldros. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Ya-rhat, the Thundercloud.

Witless Saltats (Japanese: , Dimu Sarutāto, Dim Saltat) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Saltat family, and can be found at level 31-40 at Scholes Battlegrounds in Cauldros during clear weather, rarely replacing the Strange Saltats there.

Ytterby Petramands (Japanese: , Terubimu Aranea) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Petramand family, and can be found at level 42-45 on the Alexander Ridge in Oblivia.

Yellow Arenatects (Japanese: , Iero Rorongu) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Arenatect family, and can be found at level 24-26 in the White Phosphor Lake in Cauldros. Interestingly, despite being easily distinguishable from their surroundings, they are still considered to be hidden, as they cannot be targeted outside of battle and will attack the party regardless of level.
Xe-dom Silver Crests are prime materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from silver Xe-doms. They are components in crafting the Lailah Queen and Ares 70 Skell Frames.

Young Unafulges (Japanese: , Yūsu Purumō) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Unafulge family, and can be found at level 9-10 at southwestern Seabird's Beak, located at the entrance of Sylvalum.

Ymir Gularth (Japanese: , Yumiru Gurāsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Gularth family, and can be found at level 51-80 in Cauldros during brimstone rain. They replace the Gaia Gularth. One can be found at level 65 standing by the Titan's Table, while another can be found at level 71 walking through the lava near Dragonbone Promontory.
Yamato Spirit is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Samurai Gunner at rank 10.
Yuyu is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a Ma-non and is Ackwar's lover. She can be found at the Starboard of the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles.
Xenotech Research is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from Blade HQ and the primary destination is Primordia.

Xe-dom Jet-Black Crests are prime materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from black Xe-doms. They are components in crafting the Urban Lincoln and Mastema White Reaper Skell Frames.

Xe-dom Crimson Crests are prime materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can only be obtained from Du-rha, the Imprisoned, or purchased using Reward Tickets. They are components in crafting the Formula Zero and Inferno Skydon Skell Frames.
Yusof is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found near the BLADE Tower in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles during the night.

Yin'tonam (Japanese: , In'otonamu) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is an Orphean who can be found near the BLADE Tower in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles, or at the Central Industrial District.
Wordplay is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in the Port Side corridor in the Ma-non Ship of between L and Cross at night.
Xe-dom Hands are unique materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Xe-doms. They are components in crafting the non-Ares level 60 Skell frames.
Xe-dom Golden Crests are prime materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from golden Xe-doms. They are components in crafting the Verus Cain and Amdusias Hades Skell Frames.

Yelv's Partner (Japanese: , Ieruvu no Aibō) is an Affinity Mission in . It can be accepted between the two construction cranes on North Founders Street in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles. The Mimeosome Head and Torso are received upon completion of this mission.

Wrothian Innovation (Japanese: , Shinsozai Miraniumu, The New Material Miranium) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Go Sirho in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles. Kirsty gives the Practice Data Probe during the mission. The Basic Mission Wanted: Miranium Expert can be used to locate this mission, but is not a prerequisite.
Xiphias Mine Eggs are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Xiphias.
Xenotech Survey is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from BLADE HQ and the primary destination is Noctilum.

Workout Warrior is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located across the street from Deliverance Park's southwest corner, in the Residential District of New Los Angeles between L and Cross during the early morning.

Worldly Desire is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located anytime at Ishmael Hills in the Residential District of New Los Angeles between Bozé and Cross. None of the paths in this Heart-to-Heart add affinity hearts with Bozé, but this is moot since an affinity of 5 (the maximum value) is required to access this Heart-to-Heart in the first place. Also, though all paths involve a time delay of "3 hours later," the game's day/night clock is not altered to reflect this.

Yellow Millepod Rocks are prime materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Shuravas, the Enraged, or for 198 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are one of the components of X, XV, and XX Chimeroid Slayer and Slayer.CHIMEROID augments.

Yggralith Gold is an intergalactic material in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is obtained from Appendage Fragments dropped by Yggralith Zero; if that enemy is defeated, one type of fragment is randomly chosen to be converted to the same quantity of Yggralith Gold. Yggralith Gold can also be obtained for 516 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. In it instead is available for 2565 Material Tickets from the Material Market. It is a component in the True and Infinite series of BLADE Wear.

Yggralith Horns are intergalactic materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Phanatos, the Netherlord. They are needed to craft rank X - XX Reflect Damage Up or Reflect.DAMAGE-UP augments.
Yggralith Recovery Horns are intergalactic materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Pharsis, the Everqueen.

The Xe-dom Sarto (Japanese: , Ze-raa-saruto) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Xe-dom machine, and can be found at level 55 in the White Phosphor Lake in Cauldros during The Old Gods.
Xiphias A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a blue xiphias variant. It can be obtained from Shatskikh, the Flash in Primordia.
Xiphias B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a pink xiphias variant. It can be obtained from Brandys, the Spectral Light in Sylvalum.
Wrothian Male is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a male Wrothian and can be obtained as a reward after completing Leaving the Nest.
Wrothian Female is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a female Wrothian and can be obtained as a reward after completing Until the End.
Xe-dom A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be obtained from Du-rha, the Imprisoned in Sylvalum.
Xe-dom B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be obtained from Nu-rhor, the Dark Deity in Oblivia.
Xe-dom C is a Holofigure in . It can be obtained from Gi-zho, the Iron Deity in Cauldros.
Xe-dom D is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be obtained from Go-rha, the Guardian Deity in Noctilum.

Wrath of the Keepers is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.1, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting eight Papils. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Wrecking the Ganglion is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.1, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting eight Puges. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Within the Fog is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.8, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting eighteen Adseculas. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

X-BT2 is a track in Xenoblade Chronicles X, composed and arranged by Hiroyuki Sawano. It is track five of disc four from the XenobladeX Original Soundtrack. The track is an instrumental version of Wir fliegen. It plays when Professor B uses his time machine at the end of Mystery Man.

This song does not play in the original version of the game. In the , this song plays during the flashback of when Al finds Lao in the rift between worlds, in a space the two believe to be the afterlife.

Xeno from the Abyss is a Time Attack Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked after Chapter 4 is completed, and features a level 20 version of the boss Goetia. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.
Yelv's Bodywear is Medium Wear torso armor in and . It is manufactured by Sakuraba Industries. It is part of Yelv's initial gear when he is recruited, and cannot be obtained any other way.

Workpants are Casual Wear leg armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.
Yelv's Legwear is Medium Wear leg armor in and . It is manufactured by Sakuraba Industries. It is part of Yelv's initial gear when he is recruited, and cannot be obtained any other way.
Yelv's Armwear L is Medium Wear left arm armor in and . It is manufactured by Sakuraba Industries. It is part of Yelv's initial gear when he is recruited, and cannot be obtained any other way.
Yelv's Armwear R is Medium Wear right arm armor in and . It is manufactured by Sakuraba Industries. It is part of Yelv's initial gear when he is recruited, and cannot be obtained any other way.
Youthful Hibiscuses are Casual Wear head armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are exclusively obtained from Telethia Plume.
The Youthful Sheep Horns are Casual Wear head armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Only one can be obtained per playthrough.

XSK50SA H-LARM-ATK4 is heavy left arm Skell Armor in and . It is manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.

, known in Japan as Xenoblade 2 (Japanese: , Zenobureido Tsū), is a role-playing video game published by Nintendo and developed by Monolith Soft for the Nintendo Switch. The game was announced during the Nintendo Switch Presentation on January 12, 2017. The game was released on December 1, 2017 in Japan, North America, Europe, China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. Voice Over is available in English on International cartridges and Japanese on Asian cartridges and free downloadable content for International cartridges, while text is offered in English, French, Spanish, German and Italian on International cartridges, Korean as free downloadable content for International cartridges; and Japanese, Simpli

The Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack (Japanese: , Zenobureido 2 orijinaru saundotorakku) is the album containing the musical tracks for . The music tracks of the game were composed by Yasunori Mitsuda, ACE, Kenji Hiramatsu, and Manami Kiyota. According to Yasunori Mitsuda, the soundtrack contains a total of 120 pieces. It is produced by Mitsuda's [http://www.procyon-studio.com/ Procyon Studio] and published by his own label [http://www.procyon-studio.com/sleighbells/ Sleigh Bells]. Four samples of BGM were published on the game's official [https://www.nintendo.co.jp/switch/adena/index.html Japanese] and [https://www.nintendo.co.uk/Games/Nintendo-Switch/Xenoblade-Chronicles-2-1233955.html Euro
Wrothian Parts are Important Items in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Three of them must be collected from Wrothian Skells during Prospective Partners.

Xenoblade X: The Secret File - Art of Mira is an artbook released in Japan about Xenoblade Chronicles X. It contains official art, concept art, information about the characters and enemies, and other special stories.

Young Armus (Japanese: , Yangu Aruma) are enemies in . They are members of the Armu family and can be found at level 2-3 on the Upper Level - Right area of the Gormott Province, particularly on Garanti Plain or at Lyta Oasis. They do not appear in thunderstorms. This enemy drops no items.

Yasunori Mitsuda (Japanese: , Mitsuda Yasunori) is a music composer, arranger, sound producer, and musician. He has been active in the Japanese music industry since 1992. Aside from the Xenoblade, Xenoblade 2, and Xenoblade 3 original soundtracks, his notable work comprises the Chrono Trigger, Xenogears, Xenosaga Episode I and Chrono Cross soundtracks. In 2001, Yasunori Mitsuda founded the [http://www.procyon-studio.com/ Procyon Studio] and his own label [http://www.procyon-studio.com/sleighbells/ Sleigh Bells]. They respectively produced and published the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack.

The World Tree (Japanese: , Sekaiju) is a main location in . It is a towering tree standing in the center of the endless Cloud Sea. The inhabited world of Alrest lies around it. The fabled paradise Elysium is said to be located at the top of the World Tree. The exterior of the World Tree is covered in thick growths of wood and leaves while the interior is technological-themed, a mechanical tower with robotic enemies.

The Xenoblade Chronicles 2: Sound Selection is the official soundtrack album of . It is included in the Collector's/Special Edition of the game and was released on December 1st, 2017. The soundtrack consists of thirteen songs from the game. They were composed by Yasunori Mitsuda, ACE (Tomori Kudo and CHiCO), Kenji Hiramatsu and Manami Kiyota.
Xenoblade Chronicles 2: Collected Works is an artbook for Xenoblade Chronicles 2 included with the Special Edition of the game, released on December 1st, 2017.

Xenoblade X Official Guide (, Xenoblade Cross Official Guide) is a book about Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a strategy guide which contains maps, equipment stats, enemy stats, and other useful information for players. It also includes a removable 15¾"×19¼" miniposter with maps of NLA and Mira on one side, and Collectopedia maps and information on the other side. The book was released in Japan on June 26, 2015.
Ylouz is an NPC in . Ylouz is an Urayan man who can be found on the Goldmouth Exit Dock in the Argentum Trade Guild. Ylouz offers no quests or Merc Missions.
Ysolde (Japanese: , Izorude) is an NPC in . She is an Urayan who can be found at the Central Exchange in the Argentum Trade Guild.
Wolf Fang (Japanese: , Urufufangu) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Nia's arts when using a Chroma Katana.
Woodgrain Alphorns are Instrument Pouch items in . They can be purchased at the Soniarus Music in Torigoth in the Gormott Province. They are one of Pyra's favorite Pouch items.

Wrecc Marshland (Japanese: , Rekuto Shitsugen) is a location in . It is located on the Lower Level of the Gormott Province and connects the Forgotten Waste to the rest of the Titan via Trailblazers' Bridge. There is a Treasure Trove here.
The Work Observation Tower (Japanese: , Seizō Kukaku Kanshitō) is a Location in . It is located in the Old Factory of the Empire of Mor Ardain.

Yurna the Elderwood (Japanese: , Rōne no Ōki) is a landmark in . It is a Saffronia Tree located in the Farlaine Central Pools in the Stomach of the Kingdom of Uraya. The Key to Something Key Item can be found buried in a Treasure Trove here.

The Wyrmtears (Japanese: , Ryū no Namida) is a Location in . It is located in the Stomach of Uraya, to the east of the Tardy Gate. There is an underwater spring here that connects to Badfella's Cave Fort.
Yannath Main Gate (Japanese: , Yānasu Seimon) is a Landmark in . It is located by Goetuis Port in the Indoline Praetorium.
The Womb Hollow (Japanese: , Taichū no Yokoana) is a landmark in . It is located in the Decaying Titan of the Land of Morytha, before the Central Pathway, and is what remains of Torna's Womb.

The Womb Center (Japanese: , Kyoshinjū no Tai no Chūsū) is a location in . It is located in the Decaying Titan in the Land of Morytha, between the Central Pathway and the World Tree Root. Before the Titan sank beneath the Cloud Sea, this area was known as Torna's Womb.

The World Tree Root (Japanese: , Taiju no Daikōro) is a location in . It is located at the base of the World Tree in the Land of Morytha, between the Womb Center and the Megaflote Base. There is a Collection Point and a Treasure Trove at the end of the root nearest the Womb Center. There are no enemies here.

The Wonder Spring Plaza Ruins (Japanese: , Chūfuku: Reisengai Hiroba-ato) are a landmark in . They are located on the Mid Level of Spirit Crucible Elpys, beyond the Grave Robbers' Haunt. It consists mainly of a toxic pool and stone ledges. Tunnels from here lead up to the Helical Cloister. Darkcyte can be found here during Precious Yearnings, and it must also be visited during Fool's Gold and A Secret Cure.

The Wormeater Brog (Japanese: , Wāmuītā Guroggu) is a Boss in . It is a member of the Brog family, and is fought at level 6 at Old Ghostwood Road on the Lower Level of the Gormott Province when Rex reunites with Nia.
Yumyum's Golden Gun are Literature Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Reedirait Bookstore in Goldmouth in the Argentum Trade Guild.
Woodboards are Instrument Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Soniarus Music run by Tros in Torigoth in the Gormott Province.
Woodcut Prints of Bana are Art Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Cmalaf Artwork run by Peline in Torigoth in the Gormott Province. They are wooden prints of Bana.
Wood-Carven Queens are Art Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Cmalaf Artwork in the Gormott Province.

Wood-Dye Waistclothes are Textile Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Neuromin Textiles run by Yul in the Gormott Province's Torigoth and from Silktu Textiles run by Eltetra in the Indoline Praetorium. They are one of the favorite Pouch items of Roc.
The Yafush Deeds are a Store Deed key item in . They can be purchased from Yafush Antiques in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain.
Wrapped Glarna Bakes are Staple Food Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Brad Flatforms in Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya and from Calceno Deli in the Indoline Praetorium.
Witness the Crustip are Literature Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Biblio Paulio in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal.
Yafush Antiques is a shop in . It is run by Milligan and can be found in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain. It is specialized in Art.
Yofan is an NPC in . Yofan is a Gormotti who can be found in the Gormott Province's Torigoth. Yofan runs a shop called Gryff Butchers specialized in Meats.
Yul is an NPC in . Yul is a Gormotti who can be found in the Gormott Province's Torigoth. Yul runs a shop called Neuromin Textiles specialized in Textiles.

Winter Eks (Japanese: , Wintā Ekusu) are enemies in . They are members of the Eks family, and can be found at level 5-10 on the Upper Level - Right area of the Gormott Province, particularly on Garanti Plain.

Young Eks (Japanese: , Yangu Ekusu) are enemies in . They are members of the Eks family, and can be found at level 1-4 on the Upper Level - Right area of the Gormott Province, particularly on Garanti Plain. These enemies drop no items.

Young Feris (Japanese: , Yangu Ferisu) are enemies in . They are members of the Feris family and can be found at level 3-4 on the Upper Level - Right area of the Gormott Province, usually on Garanti Plain in the company of Leo Feris. These enemies drop no items.

Yardl Krabbles (Japanese: , Yādo Kuraibu) are enemies in . They are members of the Krabble family and can be found at levels 2-8 at Torigoth in the Gormott Province and after Salvaging at Seigle Fell or Melnath's Shoulder.

Yellow Skeeters (Japanese: , Ierō Sukīto) are enemies in . They are members of the Skeeter family and can be found at level 23-24 on the Upper Level - Right of the Gormott Province. Though they only appear by themselves when it is not raining, they can emerge from Skeeter Nests in any weather.

Yolmunder's Crevasse (Japanese: , Yorumuru Kurebasu) is a location in . It is located in the southwest part of the Lower Level of the Kingdom of Tantal. A Treasure Trove is buried at the end of the small branch originating roughly in the middle of the Crevasse, it contains a Nopon Doubloon needing for the quest Nopon Doubloons Ahoy.

The Young Ardun (Japanese: , Shōnen no Arudon) is a quest-exclusive enemy in . It is a member of the Ardun family, and can be found at level 20 at Kloom Farm in the Gormott Province, after supplying Pekka with a certain amount of food for his Ardun during Ardun Rearing. This enemy will not respawn. It is recommended to not defeat the enemy, and to complete Ardun Rearing instead, to gain access to a Unique Monster Feeding the Ardun during the quest Ardun Rearing will change it to: * Infant Ardun (Lv 1) * Young Ardun (Lv 20) * Youthful Ardun (Lv 40) * Adult Ardun (Lv 60) * Ominous Ardun (Lv 80) * Relentless Arduran (Lv 99)
Young Volffs (Japanese: , Yangu Vorufu) are enemies in . They are members of the Volff family, and can be found at level 9-13 at the Sternum Arch in the Head of the Kingdom of Uraya.

Wrath Drivers (Japanese: , Rāsu Doraibā) are enemies in . They are Driver enemies, and can be found at level 97 at the Olethro Playhouse in the Kingdom of Uraya, where they assist the Unique Monster Beast-Hunter William.

Woodcutter (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when using a Ether Cannon.
Wisteria Buds are Flower collectibles in . They can be found in the Spirit Crucible Elpys.
World Supplements are Tree collectibles in . They can be found on the World Tree. In the , World Supplements can also be obtained by scanning an amiibo.
Wraithwoods are Tree collectibles in . They can be found in Temperantia.
Yehu Fishes are Fish collectibles in . They can be found by Salvaging at the Cliffs of Morytha. In the , Yehu Fishes can also be obtained by scanning an amiibo.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = World Tree Drops (Japanese: , Sekaiju no Shizuku) are accessories in . They increase all damage dealt by up to 12% for every Blade Switch performed by the wearer. This damage bonus caps at a maximum of 250% extra damage. It takes between 25 to 21 switches to fully maximize this effect, depending on the rarity of the accessory.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = World Tree Wards are accessories in . They increase the HP restored to the wearer when they are revived by up to 49% of their maximum HP. Since revivals restore 30% HP by default, these accessories allow the character to be restored with over three quarters of their HP back. They are the upgraded version of the Grandarbor Ward and Spirit Tree Ward accessories. This equipment can stack with the additive HP recovering effects of a teammate's Friendship Ring, Affection Ring or Promise Ring accessories.
Yarvay Salvaging is a shop in . It can be found in Torigoth in the Gormott Province. It is run by Heinic and is specialized in Cylinders.

Winonaite Chips are Core Chips in and . They can be obtained in Temperantia. They can be dropped by several high level enemies including Relentless Arduran and given as quest rewards for School is in Session and the DLC quest Merclibay's Mightiest. In TTGC, they can only be dropped by Mesmer Tlaloc. Winonaite Chips share their appearance with Lodranite Chips, Ureilite Chips, and Brachinite Chips. __TOC__

Wood Chips are Core Chips in and . They can be obtained from enemies in the Leftherian Archipelago and to a lesser extent the Empire of Mor Ardain, and in they can be obtained from Capital Weapons. Wood Chips share their appearance with Flower Chips, Glass Chips, and Forest Chips. __TOC__

Young Ponios (Japanese: , Yangu Ponio) are enemies in . They are members of the Ponio family, and can be found at level 19-21 at the Cargo Transportation Zone alongside Desert Ponios in the Empire of Mor Ardain.

Yumyum the Burglar is a Nopon in . He is a burglar who steals from those he feels deserve it, and views Boreas as his rival, despite his frustration of Boreas rarely listening to what he says. Yumyum's speech patterns tend more closely to normal human speech patterns than most other Nopon in the game. He appears in various locations throughout Hero of the Nopon, and can be found at the Smùide Hot Spring in Alba Cavanich, Empire of Mor Ardain upon the quest's completion.

Xenoblade 2: The Complete Guide () is a Japanese-language strategy guide for Xenoblade Chronicles 2. It contains maps and information about Blades, quests, and other details. It was released in Japan on January 20, 2018. The information in it was current as of December 22, 2017, and does not include changes due to subsequent updates or DLC.

The Yawn Lazuli is a Key Item in . It is received from Misimisi during Precious Yearnings by having him appraise a Strange Mineral from a prospecting point in Fonsett Village in the Leftherian Archipelago.

Wraithwood Roots are Key Items in . Three are scattered across the Central Plain in Temperantia. The first one is located in Toxbloom Spring, the second is located at Xataris Spring, and the third is located ahead of the Ruined Chapel of Danafas. They are required for the quest A Secret Cure.

The Youthful Ardun (Japanese: , Seinen no Arudon) is a quest-exclusive enemy in . It is a member of the Ardun family, and can be found at level 40 at the Kloom Farm in the Gormott Province, after supplying Pekka with a certain amount of food for his Ardun. (Japanese: , Zenobureido Tsū Ōgon no kuni Īra) is an expansion to and standalone game published by Nintendo and developed by Monolith Soft for the Nintendo Switch. It was first announced during the Nintendo presentation at E3 2018. It was first released as part of the Expansion Pass on September 14, 2018, with a standalone release on September 21, 2018. The standalone release is also bundled with download codes for the Expansion Pass.
